_readme: HOW NUMBERS ARE SAID (the owner, 2026-09-23: "we need to get phonetic spelling for numbers when spoken"). The script keeps its digits — captions show "$29". Only the words SENT to the voice or the song model are converted, by machine/spoken_numbers.py, and ElevenLabs' own guessing is switched off (apply_text_normalization: off), so this table is the only thing that decides how a number is said. Rules run top to bottom; a row's `examples` are checked by test_spoken.py, so change an example and the test tells you whether the machine agrees. To change how something is said: edit the words tables below (units, symbols, fixed) or the examples, then run the tests.

rules.what: whole phrases said one fixed way (the `fixed` table below)
a phone number: digit by digit, zero said "oh", a pause between groups
examples: call two oh nine, four four four, two three one six

rules.what: #1 → number one
a price range: the currency word once, at the end
examples: laser at three hundred to six hundred dollars a session

rules.what: a price. Whole dollars get the word "dollars"; dollars and cents under $1,000 are said the way a person reads a price tag ("twenty-nine ninety-nine"); cents alone are "cents"; k / M / B after the figure are thousand / million / billion; 1,100–9,999 with hundreds is said "twelve hundred"
a clock time. :00 is "o'clock" (or nothing before am/pm); :05 is "oh five"; am/pm said as letters
a score out of something: 4.9/5 → four point nine out of five
examples: four point nine out of five stars

rules.what: a simple fraction

letters said as letters, then the number: SPF 30 → S P F thirty; B3 → B three; IPX7 → I P X seven. Any 1–4 capital letters stuck to a figure are spelled out; the `letters` table lists the letter-words spelled out even with a space or no figure (SPF, UV)
two figures joined by a dash are a range: "to"
examples: one to two times a week

rules.what: 2x / 3× → two times / three times
N% → N percent
1st, 2nd, 23rd → first, second, twenty-third
a figure with k / M / B stuck to it: 40B → forty billion, 10k → ten thousand
a measurement: the unit said in full, singular for exactly one (the `units` table)
examples: three point five three fluid ounces

rules.what: a figure followed by + → "plus"
a run of five or more digits with no commas is read digit by digit (a code, a zip) — unless it ends in 00, which is a count (12000 → twelve thousand)
examples: NV eight nine one oh one

rules.what: a four-digit figure from 1100 to 2099 with no comma is read as a year
a decimal: "point", then each digit
any other whole number, commas allowed; a hyphen after it stays ("60-day" → "sixty-day")
examples: one million two hundred fifty thousand
